faqs.question: What does AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Moxifloxacin measure?
faqs.answer: This test measures the drug susceptibility of tuberculosis (TB) to the antibiotic moxifloxacin.

faqs.question: Why is AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Moxifloxacin done?
faqs.answer: • To identify drug-resistant strains of TB bacteria • To guide appropriate treatment decisions • To monitor the effectiveness of moxifloxacin in treating TB

faqs.question: When is AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Moxifloxacin recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: This test is recommended for • suspected or confirmed cases of tuberculosis, • identification of drug-resistant strains, • monitoring treatment progress and response to moxifloxacin, or • patients with a history of non-compliance to TB medications.

faqs.question: What if the results of the AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Moxifloxacin are abnormal?
faqs.answer: Abnormal results may indicate drug resistance, requiring alternate antibiotics for effective treatment.

faqs.question: What to expect during the AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Moxifloxacin?
faqs.answer: During this test, a sputum or culture sample will be collected from you. The sample will be sent to the laboratory for processing.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Moxifloxacin?
faqs.answer: • Follow any specific instructions provided by your doctor regarding diet or medication restrictions prior to the test. • Inform your doctor if you have any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Moxifloxacin?
faqs.answer: • AFB smear microscopy: This test helps in the initial detection of TB bacteria in sputum or other clinical specimens. • Drug susceptibility testing: This determines the susceptibility of TB bacteria to various antibiotics.

faqs.question: What is AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Moxifloxacin also known as?
faqs.answer: TB drug susceptibility testing for moxifloxacin

faqs.question: What is Tuberculosis (TB)?
faqs.answer: Tuberculosis (TB) is an infectious disease caused by the bacteria Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It primarily affects the lungs but can also involve other organs.
